subject.title: fix: OpenAI OAuth works behind fake-IP proxies

question: Should the narrow fake-IP exception for `auth.openai.com` apply consistently to the device-code token exchange as well as authorization-code and refresh-token exchanges?
rationale: This changes the intended SSRF exception scope for an OAuth authentication route; source evidence establishes the inconsistency, but only an owner can choose the permanent security contract.

options.title: Apply the same bounded policy to device code
options.body: Route the device-code token POST through the same exact-host policy and add focused coverage for all three OAuth exchange modes.

options.title: Keep device code fail-closed
options.body: Preserve the current device-code restriction and document that only browser OAuth token exchanges support fake-IP proxy DNS.

recommendation.title: Apply the same bounded policy to device code
recommendation.body: Route the device-code token POST through the same exact-host policy and add focused coverage for all three OAuth exchange modes.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged adjacent OAuth work recorded that fake-IP policy required a separate maintainer and security decision.
